Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No. 2525 dated 2 February 1981, made by S. Silva, Licensed Surveyor, bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama, containing in extent 10 perches, by a final decree of a partition case bearing No. 111/P dated 2 February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama.

Gamini Perera, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 March 1986, attested by R. Liyanage, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son, Suresh Perera, subject to the life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12 June 1990 due to heart failure. Vinitha revoked her life interest over the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 by Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 dated 25 February 1991, attested by S. Sapumal, Notary Public.

Suresh Perera married Kanthi and had two children, namely Rakitha and Muditha. Muditha died due to an accident on 5 June 2023, unmarried and issueless. Rakitha married Ann and died on 2 July 2022.

Suresh Perera died on 10 December 1995 intestate. Suresh Perera had an offspring named Samantha from his first marriage, who is a citizen of the United States of America.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Gamini Perera up to the present owners in relation to the land and premises bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama. **(15 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(4 marks)**
3. Can Samantha become entitled to the intestate estate of Suresh Perera? Discuss with reference to the provisions of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014, as amended by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018. **(2 marks)**
4. Explain the rules set out in sections 22 to 26 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876. **(4 marks)**

**Total: 25 marks**

claims.text: A legal pedigree showing the final devolution of title from Gamini Perera cannot be drawn up because the governing succession rules for children and other heirs (sections 23 to 26 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876) are missing from the retrieved evidence. Thus, the legal devolution upon the intestate death of Suresh Perera and the subsequent deaths of his children cannot be determined.

The precise shares presently owned by each heir cannot be calculated because the necessary succession rules (sections 23 to 26 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876) are not supplied. The only supplied rule is section 22, which states that when any person dies intestate leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property.

Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014, the transfer of title of any land in Sri Lanka to a foreigner is generally prohibited unless exempted under section 3. However, whether Samantha (a U.S. citizen) is prohibited from inheriting Suresh Perera's intestate estate cannot be fully determined because the definition of 'transfer' and the exemptions under section 3 of the Act, as well as the full text of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018, are missing.

Under section 22 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876, when any person dies intestate leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person. The rules under sections 23 to 26 of the Ordinance cannot be explained as they are missing from the provided text.

claims.text: For certain Condominium Properties owned or constructed by specific state agencies prior to December 31, 2009, the owner must submit a written declaration from the Director-General of the Department of Buildings certifying the safety of occupation at the time of registration.
The District Court of the district in which a registered Condominium Property is situated may by declaration terminate the Condominium status of such Property under specified circumstances.
A Condominium Property owner can apply to register a 'Condominium Plan' with the Registrar, submitting two copies marked 'Original' and 'Duplicate'.

The law mentions a 'Plan of redivision' and a 'Plan of amalgamation'. An owner of a unit may apply to amend a registered Condominium Plan or a registered Plan of redivision or amalgamation, which requires certification by a qualified architect or qualified civil or structural engineer if it involves survey plan alterations.
Registrations of deeds or instruments affecting units are cross-referenced with the registration of the original Condominium Plan or a Plan of redivision or amalgamation.

The heading of Section 24 refers to 'Provisions of Partition Act not to apply in certain cases', indicating restrictions on the application of partition law, but the substantive statutory rule itself is omitted from the provided text.
